title: The structure and function of G-protein-coupled receptors
authors: Rosenbaum DM, Rasmussen SG, Kobilka BK

result: Review. GPCRs are the largest family of membrane proteins and mediate most cellular responses to hormones and neurotransmitters; all have seven membrane-spanning alpha-helical segments. At the human beta2 adrenoceptor, adrenaline and noradrenaline activate the stimulatory G-protein subunit Gs alpha, which stimulates adenylyl cyclase; cAMP accumulates and activates protein kinase A, and specific phosphodiesterases lower cAMP. Activated receptors are phosphorylated by G-protein-coupled receptor kinases and bind arrestin, which prevents G-protein activation and promotes internalisation.
